trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. Its staging candidate v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error after us-east, which left the regions on mixed versions (us-east v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west v2.3.1). A retry finished the rollout. Now all three regions are on v2.3.0, healthy, with an error rate of ~0.2%. Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure (and why it was promoted even though the RC failed in staging), and look into the rollback orchestrator error.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001. The service is healthy again.

- **Rollback:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production. Since it had been healthy before, this didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Rollback problem:** The first attempt stopped after us-east because of an orchestrator error. That left us-east on v2.3.0 and the other two regions still on v2.3.1. I tried once more and it finished.
- **Current state:** All three regions are on v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2) describes the failure, the rollback and the partial failure. The request to create it timed out, so I checked before trying again: it had been created. There's only one incident, so the on-call engineer was paged once.

The incident lists follow-ups for someone to pick up:
- Find out why v2.3.1 failed, and why it went to production when its test version had already failed in staging.
- Look into the orchestrator error that stopped the first rollback.
